facts.claim: Allen calls unfinished commitments and ideas held in the head 'open loops' (also 'incompletes' or 'stuff'); keeping them in short-term memory drains the ability to concentrate on other things.
His remedy: get them out of the head into a trusted external system, and for each one decide the outcome and 'the very next action', a physical step.

Allen's image for the calm state: 'mind like water', from karate, the position of perfect readiness; a pebble thrown in a still pond makes water respond in proportion to the force, then return to calm.
facts.source: book-notes summaries; Allen's own phrase is a registered trademark

facts.claim: Allen's line 'Your mind is for having ideas, not holding them' is attributed to him; wording varies between sources.
Two-minute rule, Allen's words: 'If an action will take less than two minutes, it should be done at the moment it's defined.'

Reasoning: two minutes is 'the efficiency cutoff', the point 'where it starts taking longer to store and track an item than to deal with it.' (Allen in talk: it would take longer than two minutes to look at it again and review it.)
Before applying the rule you first decide the very next action on the item.
Caveat in the same source: do not 'become a slave to spending your day doing two-minute actions'; it applies mainly to new input. Allen also says two minutes is a guideline.
Allen's own claim in a talk: he has no backlog of two-minute items because they are all done; executives told him this habit was 'worth the price of admission'.
Weekly Review: Allen asks for a regular, preferably weekly, review of all lists; three phases named Get Clear, Get Current, Get Creative.

Get Clear: collect loose papers and materials, empty the inbox, empty your head. Get Current: review next-action lists, calendar (past and upcoming), waiting-for list, project lists. Get Creative: look over someday/maybe items.
Allen's workflow stages: collect, process, organize, review, do (2001 edition wording); the weekly review is the review stage.
Processing routine: for each inbox item decide the action; under two minutes do it, otherwise delegate or defer to a list (Allen's do/delegate/defer).
facts.source: GTD summaries; standard description of the book
